name: Enter a version
description: Recording a submission as a testing version. A submission NAMES ITS SEASON (N30): `season` is a slug, and left out it is the game's featured public season (current_season), so a client written for one season keeps working while seasons overlap. A submission is two hashes and two uploads -- there is no release and no repository, and `version` is a counter this statement assigns rather than a label the competitor types. Two statements, not one: db_write returns only rows_affected, so the row is read back, and both statements join live_sessions -- a revoked session must neither write nor read, and the read-back alone deciding 201 would fail open. The insert carries the open season's rules as PREDICATES, so a refusal is a row that was never written rather than a check that could be raced; zero rows then sends `why` to read the state back and `refused` answers 409 with one word. The duplicate refusal deliberately does not name the version it collided with: unique_weights excludes the caller, so the row it matched is always another competitor's, and naming or dating it would report one competitor's submission to another. `note` is optional: one line of up to 120 characters, public on the model page, refused on a listed word.

body.detail: weights_hash and manifest_hash are required, each as sha256:<64 hex>. Run `sha256sum model.onnx manifest.json` on the two files you are about to upload.

with.name: Both hashes, declared and well formed
with.description: `sha256:` and 71 characters, which is the shape and not the alphabet -- datalogic has no regex operator. The alphabet does not have to be checked here: the object key is a GENERATED column derived from the version id, so a hash is never a path.

with.detail: A version note is one line of at most 120 characters.
with.name: Refuse a note too long

tasks.name: Read the row back
tasks.description: Keyed on the entry id and the declared weights hash rather than a release tag: model_versions_one_in_flight_uniq makes at most one 'testing' row per entry, so the pair is unique. It is also the read-back the 401 guard rides -- a revoked session must neither write nor read, and the read-back alone deciding 201 would fail open.

tasks.name: Respond
tasks.description: 201 when the insert created the row, 200 when it did not -- which is the re-mint: the same two hashes for the version already in flight answer with fresh presigned URLs and nothing was created.

cat: PUT your two files to these URLs. They are one-shot and good for
, when this version stops waiting for them; until then, POST this submission again with the same two hashes for fresh ones.
